neet_che_u06_t08_1.working: BF3 is electron-deficient, so it accepts an electron pair (Lewis acid). It has no proton to donate, so it is not a Bronsted acid. HCl and H2O are Bronsted acids, and NH3 is a base.

neet_che_u06_t08_2.working: NH3 gains a proton to become NH4+, giving the pair NH4+/NH3. H2O loses a proton to become OH-, giving the pair H2O/OH-.

neet_che_u06_t08_3.working: HCO3- can donate a proton (forming CO3^2-) or accept one (forming H2CO3), so it is amphiprotic.

neet_che_u06_t08_4.working: A is true: NH3 accepts H+ from water. R is true: a proton acceptor must donate an electron pair to H+, so it is a Lewis base. R is only a general classification fact and does not explain why NH3 accepts a proton.

neet_che_u06_t08_5.working: Statement I is correct: Cl- is a very weak conjugate base. Statement II is incorrect: Ag+ is a Lewis acid but has no proton to donate, so it is not a Bronsted acid.
